thread:
deploy-bot: ALERT: ALB target deregistration detected for tg-edge-backends-usw2 (12 targets removed) — health checks failing with TCP RST from targets

sam: saw this correlate with the ENI failover events around 21:28 UTC, during a small infra maintenance window. ALB health checks started getting RSTs and the targets got marked unhealthy.

mira: interesting — any signs of kube-proxy restarting or iptables rules flapping?

oscar: kube-proxy stayed stable on the nodes in the logs. what *did* change was the ENI reassignment on two edge hosts (eni-0a1b2c3d) — their secondary IPs moved to a standby host.

sam: right. hypothesis: healthchecks from the ALB are SNATed by our NAT gateway/egress path and when the ENI moved the source IP map changed. ALB TCP checks got routed into the host network stack on the standby and got reset instead of reaching the pod.

mira: can we reproduce locally? any packet captures from the host showing SYN->RST?

oscar: grabbed a tcpdump from node that received the reassigned IP: ```tcpdump -nni eth0 host <alb-checker-ip> and tcp port 10256 -w /tmp/hc.pcap``` there are SYNs arriving at node but kernel sends RST quickly. looks like conntrack has a DNAT mapping pointing to old pod host.

sam: oh — conntrack DNAT pointing at the old host after ENI movement. conntrack entries not being invalidated when ENI IPs are moved between hosts. That would explain the SYN->RST for the healthcheck TCP session.

kai: low effort mitigation: increase ALB health check retries and interval to avoid flapping during ENI moves, and add a short pre-drain pause on ENI reassignment jobs. But that's a bandaid.

lisa: long term: we should ensure conntrack entries are flushed for IPs that get moved. Can we update the ENI reassignment script to run `conntrack -D -d <moved-ip>` on the target host on takeover?

oscar: yes we can. also, maybe change healthcheck source to come from ALB's dedicated IP pool that doesn't get SNATed through ENIs? Are we able to set ALB source to not be SNATed for healthchecks?

mira: ALB -> target group checks always originate from ALB nodes. Our egress path rule was causing NAT for some subnets. We can add a route so ALB healthcheck IPs bypass the NAT (preferred).

sam: immediate steps: 1) add temporary increase of healthy threshold (from 2->4) and healthy interval to 30s for tg-edge-backends-usw2; 2) push ENI reassignment job patch to run conntrack cleanup on takeover hosts; 3) add route rule to avoid SNAT for ALB healthcheck ranges.

kai: pushing step 1 now — feel free to rollback if we see more removals. :rocket:

oscar: pushed conntrack cleanup script in staging for testing. PR: `infra/eni-failover#154` (will add unit test).

lisa: i've opened a ticket to evaluate changing healthcheck source routing: INFRA-2412. mentioned the security/edge team to review routing change.

mira: after we stabilize, we should add an alert that correlates ENI reassignments + target deregistration spikes so we detect this pattern earlier.

sam: agree. also add a tiny playbook snippet for on-call: check `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces` + `conntrack -L` on affected nodes.

oscar: postmortem notes: root cause = ENI IP reassignment left stale conntrack DNAT entries causing ALB healthcheck TCP sessions to be reset by the kernel on the takeover host, triggering target deregistration.

kai: thanks all — mitigation rolling, monitoring in place. will follow up in the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
